title: Projectile Motion
description: Interactive physics simulation demonstrating parabolic trajectories of projectiles. Features controls for launch angle and velocity with visual trajectory traces and mathematical modeling of motion under gravity.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Physics
Kinematics
Projectile Motion
Gravity
Parabolic Motion
Mechanics
learningObjectives: Explain why horizontal motion proceeds at constant velocity while vertical motion accelerates under gravity, making the two components independent
Calculate the velocity components vx = v0 cos(theta) and vy = v0 sin(theta) for a given angle and power setting
Predict that a 45-degree launch angle produces maximum range in the absence of air resistance, and confirm it by firing at angles above and below 45 degrees
Compare the parabolic traces left by multiple shots to relate launch angle and power to range and peak height
Apply the kinematic equations x = x0 + vx*t and y = y0 + vy*t + 0.5*g*t^2 to describe the trajectory
